newsitem.title: CHINA: Yuan closes higher against US dollar in Shanghai.
newsitem.headline: Yuan closes higher against US dollar in Shanghai.

text.p: The Chinese yuan closed slightly up at 8.2970 against the U.S. dollar on Friday from Thursday's 8.2974 on the Shanghai-based interbank foreign exchange market, traders said.
The yuan opened unchanged at 8.2974 and consolidated around 8.2970 for most of the session, hitting an intra-day high of 8.2966 and a low of 8.2977.
Trading was dull with most done at 8.2970, partly because of the too stable movement of the yuan, dealers said.
"Several banks sold dollars to try to push the price higher, but the yuan was firmly capped at 8.2970," one dealer said.
"The movement of the yuan over the past week has been similar to that in July last year when it consolidated around the 8.30 level for a long time," a second dealer said.
"The trend indicates the market has no clear idea about the yuan's longer-term direction," he said.
Dealers expect the yuan to rise steadily early next week.
The yuan fell to close at 7.3900 from 7.3700 against 100 Japanese yen and slightly up at 1.0736 from 1.0738 against the Hong Kong dollar.
